text:
sarah: Quick sync — need to finalize enforcement checklist for how plan quotas are shown in the Console and where enforcement happens (edge proxy vs internal quota service). Main points: soft-exhaustion warnings in UI, hard throttle triggers, per-key cooldown semantics, and telemetry events for billing. @anita @mike

mike: Agree. My proposal: UI shows a softcap status at 75% of monthly allowance, and a hardcap at 100%. Softcap = visual warning + email/operator webhook. Hardcap = enforcement at the edge proxy (fast fail).

anita: From product POV we also want a grace buffer for enterprise: allow a configurable burst of +10% for Enterprise with billing alert. Free plans get immediate hardcap at 100%. Pro gets 24h soft-grace (automated throttle rampdown).

josh: Billing needs telemetry events named quota.soft_exhaust and quota.hard_exhaust with these fields: org_id, plan, window_start, window_end, tokens_used, tokens_allowed. We need those for invoicing overages and alerts.

sarah: Good — where should enforcement live? Edge proxy has lowest latency but harder to change behavior per-plan. Internal quota service is flexible but adds a hop. Thoughts on hybrid?

mike: Hybrid is best: edge does fast checks against cached per-org tokens (short TTL, ~15s) and falls back to central quota service when cache miss or for policy decisions (e.g., enterprise burst). That lets us do hard throttle with <10ms p99 on cache hit.

quota-bot: automated note: cache-ttl = 15s recommended. Remember to instrument cache hit/miss rates.

anita: UX details: Console quota card should show: current usage (tokens), percent of monthly plan, softcap flag, projected trend (12h/3d), and recommended action (upgrade / request burst). Show a timestamp for last sync.

devex: Can we add a small inline CTA for quick increase requests that creates a ticket? For enterprise, CTA should propose an immediate temporary +burst for 24h pending approval.

mike: Implementation checklist (engineering):
- edge token bucket enforcement with per-key counters and cache fallback
- central quota service supports overrides (burst, exemptions, per-org configs)
- metric emissions: quota.check, quota.decision, quota.enforcement, quota.cache_hit/miss
- rate-limit headers on responses: X-RW-Quota-Remaining, X-RW-Quota-Reset, X-RW-Plan

sarah: On headers: please keep them small and stable. Example header proposal:```
X-RW-Quota-Remaining: 12345
X-RW-Quota-Reset: 1700000000
X-RW-Plan: pro
```

mike: Also recommend a cooldown semantic for per-key bursts: when a key exceeds softcap but under hardcap, start a gradual token refill penalty (reduce refill rate by 50% for N minutes) rather than an immediate block. For free keys we skip the cooldown and block at hardcap.

anita: That cooldown behavior should be documented in Console help and exposed as a small tooltip on the quota card.

josh: For billing, we need an event when refill penalty is applied (quota.penalty_applied) so finance can correlate to usage anomalies.

quota-bot: automated note: add telemetry tag plan_tier=free|pro|enterprise to all quota events.

mike: Rollout plan: staged rollout by org size. Phase 1: internal + 5 test customers (no hard throttles, simulate enforcement). Phase 2: 10% of orgs get softcap warnings + visual UI. Phase 3: enable edge enforcement for free/pro with hard throttles. Phase 4: enterprise opt-in for burst billing.

sarah: Can someone own the Console copy and help text for soft vs hard caps? @devex

devex: I can draft copy. Proposed short lines: "Soft cap: you're nearing your monthly quota — we will slow requests to preserve service. Hard cap: your plan limit has been reached and requests will be blocked." Will add CTA flows.

anita: One more: migration safety — for existing customers we should preserve their current per-org allowances and not start hard enforcement until next billing cycle unless they opt in.

mike: Agreed. Flag in central service: enforcement_enabled = false for legacy orgs until migration date.

sarah: Okay action items: @mike implement edge cache + headers PoC, @josh add telemetry schema, @devex draft Console copy, @anita finalize plan burst rules, I'll prepare rollout announcement and migration schedule.

mike: I'll open a PR with the PoC and a small load test (focus on cache hit p99 < 10ms).

josh: I'll publish telemetry schema in telemetry repo and add the billing consumers.

quota-bot: automated reminder: please add unit tests for quota.decision logic and integration test for cache fallback.

sarah: Thanks everyone — we'll reconvene after PR and telemetry schema are up. :thumbsup:
